subject: src/tensorlbm/contact_angle_inversion/ (m18090 deliverable: calibrate/invert/forward)
why: m18090 validated the calibrated inversion on 3 hold-out angles at ONE configuration (nx=128, ny=64, G=5, tau=1.0).
Its own coarse calibration table is NON-MONOTONE in cos(f_w) near f_w=0.60-0.65, so the delivered invert() (first-bracket search) has more than one solution there - never tested.
No published evidence that a coarse calibration transfers to (a) the production grid or (b) a different viscosity (tau).

A_inband_coarse.note: same config as the calibration (coarse), target angles placed inside / next to the ambiguous band

B_fine_transfer.note: calibration from the coarse grid applied on the production grid (resolution transfer)

C_tau_transfer.note: calibration from tau=1.0 applied at tau=1.2 (viscosity/transport transfer; a static angle must not care)

gates.gate_source: owner precision standard (error > 15% is unacceptable); m18090 acceptance uses the same gate
gates.G1_inband: every Arm A row with status ok must satisfy |theta_measured - theta_target| / theta_target < 15% AND converge (tail drift <= 1 deg).
gates.G2_resolution_transfer: every Arm B row < 15%. If it fails, the deliverable's inversion is NOT portable in resolution and the failure is reported as an honest negative (no recalibration added in this round).
gates.G3_tau_transfer: every Arm C row < 15% (a static contact angle must be independent of tau).
gates.H1_branch: if the coarse calibration is non-monotone at the evaluated target, BOTH inversion branches are run; the branch spread |theta_first - theta_last| is reported as the inversion ambiguity of the delivered calibrate/invert pair (no pass/fail gate: this is a diagnostic).
gates.measurability: a row whose measurement returns status != ok, or whose tail drift > 1 deg, is reported as NOT_MEASURED and excluded from the pass counts (never counted as a pass).

honesty_rules: no hand-copied numbers: every table in REPORT.md is rendered from summary.json, produced by run_xval.py report
no identity checks: the error is always measured-from-LBM minus target, never forward(invert(theta))
an arm that fails is reported as FAIL, not dropped
